about: A personal tracker of clinical neuropsychology research and UK practice developments, with a dedicated section on motor neurone disease. Each item is a neutral summary of a published study or public document: for research, the design, findings and stated limitations; for policy, what it says, who it affects and when. Every item links to its source.
coverage_note: Seed edition covering publications up to 26 October 2026, weighted to the preceding three months. Updated every Monday.
ahead_blurb: Conferences, decision dates, deadlines and expected trial readouts across all three sections.

trackers.name: Deprivation of liberty after the AGNI judgment, and the Liberty Protection Safeguards
trackers.stage_label: New legal test in force; government guidance interim
trackers.summary: The Supreme Court replaced the Cheshire West acid test in June 2026. DoLS remains the authorisation scheme in England and Wales; the Liberty Protection Safeguards, legislated in 2019, have never been brought into force.
points: Whether arrangements amount to a deprivation of liberty is now a multifactorial judgment about the person's concrete situation, not a single acid test.

A person lacking capacity on residence and care can give subjective consent (awareness, basic understanding, acceptance) that takes the arrangements outside Article 5; serious doubt means consent cannot be concluded.
DHSC guidance asks bodies to review existing DoLS authorisations as soon as practicable, and to take a cautious approach to borderline cases in the short term.
The 2008 DoLS Code of Practice was republished on 2 June 2026 but does not fully reflect the new test.

updates.title: Neuropsychiatric symptom networks largely overlap in early- and late-onset Alzheimer's disease
updates.summary: Network analysis of NPI-Q data from 1,360 people in the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort found similar overall structure in early- and late-onset AD, with aggression central in both but linked to different symptoms.
updates.design: 655 early-onset (<65; mean age 58.4) and 705 late-onset (≥65; mean 70.8) AD. NPI-Q items dichotomised and modelled as Ising networks; groups compared with the Network Comparison Test.
points: Apathy and depression were the most prevalent symptoms in both groups (EOAD 58% and 48%; LOAD 55% and 43%).
Global network strength did not differ significantly between groups.
EOAD: strongest edges aggression–disinhibition and aggression–irritability; most central nodes aggression and anxiety.
LOAD: strongest edge depression–anxiety; most central nodes aggression and disinhibition.
caveats: Cross-sectional: edges describe conditional co-occurrence, not causal pathways.
Informant questionnaire items were dichotomised, so severity was not modelled.
Single memory-clinic cohort.

links.label: Weltings et al., Alzheimer's Research & Therapy (2026)

updates.title: How memory-clinic clinicians communicate neuropsychological assessment results
updates.summary: Focus groups with Dutch memory-clinic physicians and psychologists describe neuropsychological assessment as central to diagnostic disclosure, with communication tailored to patient and carer.
updates.design: Four focus groups (two physician, two psychologist) with experienced clinicians; deductive thematic content analysis by two independent researchers. Participant total not given in the abstract.
points: Neuropsychological results were integrated with other diagnostic tests and central to disclosure conversations.
Clinicians adapted communication to patient and caregiver characteristics, using strategies to aid understanding and manage emotional reactions.
Participants favoured personalised, structured disclosures.
Acceptance was seen as extending beyond the clinic, but disclosure was felt to shape early understanding and adjustment.
caveats: Clinician perspective only; patients and carers were not interviewed.
Dutch memory-clinic setting.

links.label: Stolte et al., BMC Geriatrics (2026)

updates.title: Emotion regulation difficulties track executive and initiation apathy in Huntington's disease
updates.summary: In 89 HD gene expansion carriers, DERS scores were most strongly associated with Dimensional Apathy Scale executive and behaviour/initiation subscales, independent of depression; emotional apathy was not significantly associated.
updates.design: Copenhagen. 89 carriers (48 premanifest, 41 manifest); no control group. DERS, LARS, Dimensional Apathy Scale, HAM-17 as covariate, MoCA/MMSE.
points: DERS correlated with LARS global apathy (rs = 0.39), DAS executive (rs = 0.60) and behaviour/initiation apathy (rs = 0.55).
DAS emotional apathy was not significantly associated with DERS (rs = 0.22, p = 0.068).
After adjusting for depression, executive plus behaviour/initiation apathy explained an additional 24.2% of DERS variance (p < 0.001).
Exploratory: executive apathy was independently associated with DERS in premanifest (β = 0.437, p = 0.006) but not manifest carriers.
caveats: Authors note the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-report and small exploratory subgroups.

links.label: Poulsen et al., Journal of Neurology (2026)

updates.title: CCAS-Scale shows moderate responsiveness after acute cerebellar stroke
updates.summary: In 21 patients with first-ever cerebellar stroke, Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome Scale scores rose by a median of one point between day 7 and discharge (SRM 0.52).
updates.design: Single-centre prospective observational study. Assessed 7 days after onset and at discharge (median 21 days later) with the CCAS-Scale, MMSE, SARA and FIM.
points: Median CCAS-Scale score 71 → 72 (p = 0.018); failed items 4 → 3 (p = 0.035).
Definite CCAS fell from 81.0% to 66.7%; every patient still met at least possible CCAS at discharge.
CCAS-Scale SRM 0.52 (95% CI 0.20–0.88); SARA and FIM showed large responsiveness, MMSE small.
CCAS-Scale change correlated with FIM change (rho = 0.44, p = 0.046), not with SARA or MMSE change.
caveats: Authors caution that a one-point median change and a wide SRM confidence interval leave clinical significance uncertain.
Small single-centre sample; short follow-up; abstract only (full text paywalled).

links.label: Shinya et al., The Cerebellum (2026)

updates.title: Lesion-derived connectivity estimates predict four-year SDMT in multiple sclerosis
updates.summary: Structural and functional connectivity estimated from clinical MRI lesion masks predicted follow-up Symbol Digit Modalities Test scores in 171 people with MS (median Spearman ρ 0.56–0.58).
updates.design: 171 people with MS, cognition at baseline and 4 years. Structural connectivity estimated from lesion masks (Network Modification tool); functional connectivity then estimated with an encoder–decoder model (Krakencoder). Outcome: SDMT.
points: Prediction was best for follow-up SDMT using regional estimated structural (ρ 0.58) or functional (ρ 0.56) connectivity.
Lower estimated cerebellar connectivity was associated with lower follow-up SDMT.
Higher estimated default-mode functional connectivity was associated with lower follow-up SDMT.
caveats: Connectivity is estimated from lesion maps, not measured with diffusion or functional imaging.
Single cognitive outcome (SDMT); the authors' summary describes predictive performance as moderate.

links.label: Tozlu et al., Nature Communications (2026)

updates.title: Cognitive decline after frontal glioma treatment tracks white-matter change
updates.summary: In 40 patients with frontal lobe glioma, MoCA fell from 25.3 before surgery to 23.9 six months after radiotherapy; FA change in specific tracts tracked change in matching cognitive domains.
updates.design: Retrospective, single centre. MoCA and DTI (FA, MD in seven tracts) before surgery, one month after surgery, and six months after radiotherapy.
points: MoCA 25.34 ± 2.20 → 25.15 ± 2.47 → 23.87 ± 2.91 (p < 0.001); declines in visuospatial/executive and delayed recall items.
SLF, cingulum and corpus callosum showed FA decreases and MD increases, largest at the final time point.
FDR-corrected correlations: corpus callosum FA with MoCA total (r = 0.57); SLF with visuospatial/executive (r = 0.41); cingulum with delayed recall (r = 0.39).
Tract changes were not associated with extent of resection or radiation dose.
caveats: Retrospective, n = 40, MoCA as the only cognitive measure.

links.label: Chen et al., BMC Medical Imaging (2026)

updates.title: Loneliness linked to smaller CA3 volume only in pTau217-positive older adults
updates.summary: Baseline IGNITE data (582 with plasma pTau217) showed loneliness associated with smaller total hippocampal volume, and with smaller CA3 only among pTau217-positive participants.
updates.design: Baseline of IGNITE, a 12-month aerobic exercise trial in cognitively unimpaired adults aged 65–80. Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale; 3T hippocampal subfield MRI (ASHS); plasma pTau217 (ALZpath, positive >0.46 pg/mL).
points: Loneliness was associated with smaller total hippocampal volume (β = −0.077, p = 0.031; about −61 mm³ per SD).
No main effects on individual subfields.
Loneliness × pTau217 interaction for CA3 (β = −0.215, p = 0.012): inverse association in pTau217-positive (β = −0.230) but not negative participants.
Subfield interactions did not survive FDR correction at 0.05.
caveats: Authors describe effects as modest and state the findings do not establish clinical significance.
Cross-sectional; sample 72% female and 76% White.

links.label: Martín-Fuentes et al., GeroScience (2026)

updates.title: Three or more concussions associated with higher depressive symptoms in recently retired college footballers
updates.summary: Among 627 former US collegiate football players surveyed within five years of leaving the sport, those reporting 3+ lifetime concussions had higher PHQ-9 scores than those reporting none.
updates.design: CARE Consortium, 26 US universities; mean age 25. Outcomes: Neuro-QoL Cognitive, PHQ-9, SF-12 MCS, Satisfaction with Life Scale. Exposures: lifetime concussions (0, 1–2, 3+), playing position, years played.
points: Adjusted: 3+ concussions associated with higher PHQ-9 versus none (B = 1.53, p = 0.014).
The SF-12 MCS difference did not survive multiple-comparison correction.
1–2 concussions did not differ from none; years of participation showed no associations.
Line players had the highest proportion with PHQ-9 ≥ 10 (17.8%).
caveats: All outcomes and concussion history self-reported; no performance-based cognitive testing.
Position and years played used as proxies for head-impact exposure.
Cross-sectional design.

links.label: Syrydiuk et al., Sports Medicine – Open (2026)

updates.title: Active Brains: online cognitive and lifestyle support for older adults with cognitive impairment
updates.summary: A community-based UK trial in more than 11,500 people aged 60–85 compared brief advice with a brain-training website, with or without brief facilitator support, over 12 months.
updates.design: Three arms: control (cognitive testing plus brief lifestyle advice); website (brain exercises and advice); website plus two brief facilitator contacts, usually a nurse. 12-month follow-up.
points: University of Southampton release: 28% of the control group no longer met criteria for cognitive impairment at 12 months.
The release reports 8% (website) and 18% (facilitator-supported) reductions in mild cognitive impairment compared with control.
Investigators attribute the effect to brain-stimulating activity; most participants already reported reasonably healthy activity and diet.
caveats: Figures come from the university press release; check the paper for the primary outcome, whether reductions are absolute or relative, and confidence intervals.

links.label: The Lancet Primary Care — Active Brains trial
University of Southampton news release (28 Sep 2026)

updates.title: Functional cognitive disorder in two memory clinics in Côte d'Ivoire
updates.summary: 10.2% of 244 memory-clinic patients met criteria for functional cognitive disorder; most were referred for memory complaints and over half had a comorbid mental health disorder.
updates.design: Retrospective records review, two private memory clinics in Abidjan, 2018–2023. FCD required normal neurological examination and MRI plus internal inconsistency between reported symptoms and test performance.
points: 25 of 244 met criteria; mean age 45.8; 56% university-educated.
Mental health comorbidity in 52% (depression 36%).
Mean MoCA 23.2 ± 5.9; most points lost on memory, attention and visuospatial/executive items; naming and orientation best preserved.
Mean delay from symptom onset to consultation: 29.9 months.
caveats: Authors cite the small sample, retrospective design and lack of established diagnostic criteria.
MoCA was the only cognitive measure reported.

links.label: Kouassi et al., Frontiers in Neurology (2026)

updates.title: AD-SMART platform trial opens to test metformin and atomoxetine in Alzheimer's disease
updates.summary: A UK multi-arm, multi-stage platform modelled on MND-SMART will compare repurposed drugs with a shared placebo in about 1,200 people, starting with metformin and atomoxetine.
updates.design: Adaptive platform; arms dropped and replaced at interim analyses. Eligibility: age 55+ with Alzheimer's or mixed Alzheimer's/vascular dementia; standard treatments may continue. Assessments at baseline, 6, 12 and 18 months, including cognition, daily activities, MRI and blood biomarkers.
points: Recruiting at Cambridgeshire & Peterborough and Surrey & Borders NHS trusts; open at Imperial, Edinburgh and Southampton; more than 30 sites planned.
Led by the UK Dementia Research Institute and Alzheimer's Research UK, with Imperial, UCL's trials unit, Oxford and Dementias Platform UK.
Evaluation of the first two drugs expected to finish around 2030.
updates.who: Referral routes: Join Dementia Research or the Dementia Research Infoline (0300 111 5 111).

updates.title: Supreme Court overrules Cheshire West and resets the deprivation of liberty test
updates.summary: In the AGNI Reference [2026] UKSC 16 the court set aside the Cheshire West acid test and held that a person lacking capacity to decide on residence and care can still consent to arrangements in a way that takes them outside Article 5.
points: Unanimous seven-justice court; judgment by Lord Sales and Lady Simler.

Replaces the acid test with a multifactorial assessment of the person's concrete situation: supervision and control, ability to leave, type, duration, effects and purpose of restrictions, and the person's own experience.
Subjective consent has a lower threshold than MCA capacity: awareness of the environment, a basic understanding of the circumstances and acceptance, which can be tacit.
Objection and the person's wishes and feelings are relevant again; compliance alone does not establish consent.
updates.who: Anyone assessing capacity or contributing evidence to DoLS authorisations and Court of Protection applications, including neuropsychological capacity assessments and records of the person's wishes and feelings.
updates.dates: Judgment 2 June 2026; effective immediately across the UK.

links.label: 39 Essex Chambers — case summary of [2026] UKSC 16

updates.title: DHSC guidance on applying the 2026 deprivation of liberty test
updates.summary: Government guidance, first published 15 June and last updated 22 September 2026, sets out how health and care bodies should apply the AGNI judgment, including reviewing existing DoLS authorisations.
points: A person who lacks capacity may still validly consent if they can express wishes and feelings; where there is serious doubt, valid consent cannot be concluded.
Authorisations are expected to fall substantially over time, but a cautious approach is advised for now, with borderline cases referred for review.
Existing authorisations for people no longer deprived of liberty should be reviewed as soon as practicable; leaving them in place meanwhile is not unlawful.
The 2008 DoLS Code was republished on 2 June 2026; its chapter 2 does not fully reflect the new test.
NHS England updated its MCA/DoLS e-learning on 30 July 2026, with revised materials due by December 2026.
caveats: DHSC says further interim guidance, including case studies, will follow.
updates.who: Local authorities, NHS trusts and practitioners involved in DoLS, community deprivation of liberty and capacity assessment.
updates.dates: First published 15 June 2026; last updated 22 September 2026.

updates.title: £80m Dementia Challenge to test faster diagnosis tools in the NHS, including remote cognitive assessment
updates.summary: UKRI is funding nine projects for staged real-world NHS testing, aiming for 92% of people to be diagnosed within 18 weeks of referral (around 60% now).
points: Cognitive assessment projects: a 15-minute remote digital cognitive assessment (Cognitron), a digital cognitive-monitoring platform (Exeter), and a home auditory-processing test (Queen Mary).

Other projects: faster MRI (about 20 to 7 minutes; UCL/UK DRI), a blood biomarker panel in routine memory services (Oxford/DPUK), home sensor monitoring (Minder, Imperial), sleep apnoea screening (Bristol), an AI progression tool (Cambridge), and redesign of Scottish diagnostic services (Edinburgh).
Only projects that show results receive further funding.

updates.title: Mild cognitive impairment in presymptomatic carriers of ALS-associated variants
updates.summary: In the Pre-fALS cohort, 14% of at-risk participants met MCI criteria at one or more visits, mainly in executive function and language, compared with 4% of non-carriers.
updates.design: Pre-symptomatic Familial ALS (Pre-fALS) study, North America: asymptomatic people at genetic risk of ALS/FTD, with non-carriers blinded to status as controls. Neuropsychological data from 216 participants over 807 visits (data cut May 2024). Authors: McHutchison, Abrahams, Benatar et al.
points: 31 participants (14%) met MCI criteria at one or more visits (4% of all visits).
By genotype: C9orf72 20% (15/74), SOD1 13% (12/94), other variants 15% (3/20), non-carriers 4% (1/28).
Impairment mainly affected executive function and language.
Classification often changed between visits.
The study's criteria flagged fewer impaired visits than the revised Strong criteria developed for symptomatic ALS.
caveats: Figures here are from a secondary report of the paper; check the article for exact definitions and analyses.
Small non-carrier comparison group (n = 28).

updates.title: Alzheimer's co-pathology markers and cognition in ALS
updates.summary: In 192 people with ALS or ALS-FTD, CSF p-tau and total tau were associated with domain-specific ECAS performance; plasma extracellular-vesicle TDP-43 and NfL showed weak or no association.
updates.design: 192 ALS/ALS-FTD and 100 healthy controls. CSF total tau, p-tau and β-amyloid; plasma EV TDP-43 and NfL; ECAS. Post-mortem data for a subset. Kasper, Hermann et al.
points: AD-related biomarkers were elevated versus controls, especially in ALS with cognitive impairment (ALSci) and ALS-FTD.
β-amyloid differed between controls and ALSci, but not between controls and cognitively unimpaired ALS.
CSF p-tau and t-tau were strongly associated with domain-specific cognition.
Post-mortem: ABC scores and overall TDP-43 burden were not strongly associated with cognitive state; temporal and hippocampal TDP-43 burden was.
caveats: In-vivo biomarkers distinguished impairment only in ALSci and ALS-FTD.
Autopsy data for a subset only; effect sizes not given in the abstract.
updates.dates: Annals of Neurology vol. 100, issue 1 (July 2026), pp. 123–138.

updates.title: At-home EEG and gamified cognitive testing feasible over eight months in ALS and FTD
updates.summary: 11 people with ALS, 7 with FTD and 10 controls completed fortnightly home sessions with a dry-sensor EEG headset and tablet tasks, benchmarked against the ECAS and a full neuropsychological battery.
updates.design: CNS-102, Beaumont Hospital Dublin / Trinity College Dublin (PI Orla Hardiman). Fortnightly home sessions (16-channel dry EEG, 10 tablet tasks); in-clinic assessment at baseline, 4 and 8 months.
points: Usability good to excellent; ALS group mean System Usability Scale 89.
At baseline, home measures separated ALS, FTD and control groups with effect sizes comparable to the benchmark tests.

Exploratory: four home measures showed group × time interactions, including decline in ALS on facial-expression recognition and speech fluency; the in-clinic battery showed no significant group-level change over the same period.
caveats: Proof-of-concept sample of 28; authors call for larger cohorts.
Platform developer and a pharmaceutical consortium (Biogen, Boehringer Ingelheim, BMS, Lilly, GSK, Takeda) involved; details here are from the developer's summary.

updates.title: Plasma protein panel estimates timing of ALS onset in genetic-risk carriers
updates.summary: In Pre-fALS, a 19-protein plasma panel including NfL predicted phenoconversion over horizons of six months to five years, estimating onset to within about two years.
updates.design: Olink proteomics (over 5,000 proteins) on longitudinal plasma from 137 Pre-fALS participants, 33 of whom developed ALS or FTD; tested in UK Biobank. Ran, Wuu, Benatar et al.
points: 92 proteins differed before symptom onset.
Machine-learning models selected a 19-protein panel including NfL.
Estimated onset fell within two years of actual symptom onset; similar results in UK Biobank.
caveats: Genetically at-risk cohort with 33 phenoconverters; performance in sporadic ALS not established.

updates.title: Higher nano- and microplastic levels in CSF and blood of newly diagnosed ALS
updates.summary: An Italian case–control study of 24 people with newly diagnosed ALS and 20 controls found higher particle concentrations in CSF and blood in ALS, with no association with progression.
updates.design: 24 newly diagnosed ALS, 20 controls; nano- and microplastics quantified in blood and CSF.
points: Median CSF levels exceeded 1,000 particles/mL in ALS, versus under 300 (men) and 700 (women) particles/mL in controls.
Blood differences were smaller; the association with ALS appeared only above a threshold level.
No association with disease progression.
caveats: Association only: reverse causation and other environmental exposures not excluded.
Small sample; details here are from a news report of the paper.

updates.title: Ulefnersen meets primary endpoint in phase 3 FUSION trial for FUS-ALS
updates.summary: Intrathecal ulefnersen improved a joint rank of ALSFRS-R change, time to rescue and ventilation-free survival versus placebo at 72 weeks (p = 0.0005; n = 73).
updates.design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1–3 study in FUS-ALS; 72-week double-blind period, then open-label extension.
points: Primary endpoint met (p = 0.0005).
Company reports significant improvements in serum NfL and in time to death, permanent ventilation, rescue or withdrawal for progression.
Most adverse events mild or moderate; no detailed safety data released.
Otsuka plans expedited regulatory discussions; an early access programme is open to eligible patients.
caveats: Topline company data; full results not yet presented or peer reviewed.
FUS variants are thought to cause under 1% of MND.

updates.title: AP-101 (misfolded-SOD1 antibody): phase 3 planned for 2027
updates.summary: AL-S Pharma will present post-hoc phase 2 body-weight analyses at NEALS and has outlined a phase 3 trial of about 300 people with ALS starting in 2027.
points: Phase 2 (n = 73) met its primary safety and tolerability endpoint; no anti-drug antibodies reported.
Post-hoc weight analyses favoured AP-101 (e.g. 4.82 kg difference in SOD1-ALS at follow-up, p = 0.0092); reductions in serum NfL and CSF pNfH reported in the per-protocol population.
Phase 3 design: 2:1 randomisation, 2,500 mg IV every three weeks for 12 months; joint ALSFRS-R and death/permanent ventilation analysis; onset within 24 months and SVC ≥ 60%.
caveats: Weight findings are post hoc and come from a company release.
updates.dates: NEALS presentation 28 October 2026; phase 3 start planned for 2027.
